live.name: GOLD HARVEST
live.headline: GOLD HARVEST: a threat actor tracked under several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists GOLD HARVEST under five other names and names three remote-access tools tied to it. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: The catalogue record, sourced to Secureworks, tracks the actor as GOLD HARVEST.
The same record lists these aliases: Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
The record lists three tools: AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: GOLD HARVEST
next.headline: GOLD HARVEST (Scattered Spider): a help-desk and phone-scam crew that goes after IT support and outsourcers
next.in_short: GOLD HARVEST is the Secureworks name for the group also known as Scattered Spider. Vendors describe a financially motivated actor that uses social engineering to get past MFA, and that has worked with ransomware operators.

sentences.t: GOLD HARVEST is the Secureworks name for a group also tracked as Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
CrowdStrike calls Scattered Spider a prolific eCrime adversary that has run financially motivated activity since early 2022.
Check Point Research says the group has been active since at least 2022 and is made up mainly of young people aged 19 to 22 from the US and UK.
ReliaQuest says there is plenty of circumstantial evidence of a deliberate partnership between ShinyHunters and Scattered Spider. It describes both as linked to a wider network called The Com.

Trustwave SpiderLabs says a brand called Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters appeared on Telegram in early August 2025, borrowing the names of Scattered Spider, ShinyHunters and LAPSUS$. It does not treat the brand as a formal, centralized organization.
CrowdStrike says the group's early campaigns reportedly targeted customer relationship management and business-process outsourcing firms, plus telecommunications and technology companies.
ReliaQuest reports that 70% of the group's targets are in technology, finance and retail trade.

Halcyon says the group compromises call centers and other outsourcing providers to reach many victims at once. It assesses that attacks on UK retail and US insurance likely began, at least in part, with such compromises.
Check Point Research says the group is now also targeting aviation alongside enterprises. It bases the airline link on media reports and intelligence advisories.
Mandiant reports that UNC3944 targets IT help desks to get around multifactor authentication.
ReliaQuest says the group relies on phishing, voice phishing and help-desk impersonation. It also uses phishing frameworks such as Evilginx to bypass MFA.
Check Point Research lists SIM swapping and MFA fatigue ("push bombing") among the group's techniques.
Halcyon says the group has consistently used insider recruitment. It says the group impersonates IT staff and guides users to download remote access tools such as AnyDesk or ScreenConnect.
The catalogue record lists AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein as tools linked to the group.
ReliaQuest says the group has alliances with ransomware operators ALPHV, RansomHub and DragonForce. BleepingComputer's report says it has also partnered with Qilin.
Sygnia names Scattered Spider among the groups that attack VMware ESXi virtualization environments.
BleepingComputer says that in September 2023 the group breached MGM Resorts by impersonating an employee. It then encrypted over 100 VMware ESXi hypervisors with BlackCat ransomware.
ReliaQuest notes that a wave of attacks hit UK retailers in May 2025, including Marks & Spencer, Co-op and Harrods. It says nothing definitive has tied those incidents to Scattered Spider.
BleepingComputer reports that an Aflac spokesperson could not attribute that insurer's breach to a group. The report says the breach shows all the signs of a Scattered Spider attack.
Cybersecurity Dive says researchers cite increasing evidence of collaboration between Scattered Spider and ShinyHunters. The article was about a social engineering campaign that Workday confirmed.

Rapid7 investigated an April 2026 intrusion that began with a Teams message from a fake IT Support account. It says the approach mirrors tradecraft seen in Octo Tempest-style campaigns, and does not describe this as a confirmed link.
Resecurity does not believe the announced retirement of the Scattered Spider, LAPSUS$ and ShinyHunters alliance is sincere.
Treat password and MFA reset requests to the help desk as high-risk. Confirm the caller through a second, known channel before acting.
Check the security of outsourced support providers, and limit which remote access tools staff may install.
